4.title: How This Solo AI Founder Bootstrapped 5 Products to 1M+ / Month | Tibo Louis-Lucas
4.author: Peter Yang
4.hook: Solo founder's playbook for validating AI products fast, acquiring users, and pricing — with 5 products to $1M+/month as proof.

5.title: My Simple Claude Cowork System (for normal people)
5.author: Jeff Su
5.hook: A three-level workspace architecture for Claude with persistent memory, instruction files, and concrete use cases (email, spending tracking, newsletter drafting).

6.title: Speech-to-Speech Model Research at Google DeepMind — Valeria Wu Fon & Tom Ouyang, Google DeepMind
6.author: AI Engineer
6.hook: Google DeepMind's speech-to-speech model handles code-switching and multimodal input natively, but exposes a three-way tension between conversational latency, task intelligence, and multimodal capability.

1.title: AI Engineer Paris 2026 Main Stage: Google DeepMind, ElevenLabs, Hugging Face & Stripe | Day 2 2026-09-24 12:00
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Multi-track technical deep-dives on production AI systems from builders at scale (model inference, voice/realtime, agents, edge AI, economics).

1.title: World Models Need Causality, Not Pretty Pixels — Christopher Manning, Moonlake AI
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Manning argues that effective world models need causal structure (action-conditioned simulation in code) not pixel generation, and Moonlake demonstrates this by building interactive 3D worlds from photos, filling in occluded details via web research, and using a Claude Code–inspired loop to close the sim-to-real gap.

1.title: Physical AI's Next Bottleneck Is Finding the Right Video — Rafael Levi, Bright Data
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Video indexing by action (not title) cuts training data waste from 96% to viable levels, with Bright Data's API returning trimmed clips + timestamps; Meta's case: 1M hours public video + 62 hours real robot data.

2.title: I Gave an AI a Body — Cyrus Clarke, MIT Media Lab
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: MIT researcher built a closed-loop system that trained an AI-controlled shape display to develop 32 gestural "answers" faster than language output, starting from zero instruction.

3.title: One Operator, Many Drones: Inside Skydio's Autonomy Stack — Suchet Bargoti, Skydio
3.author: AI Engineer
3.hook: VLM agents replacing hand-coded rules for autonomous drone tracking, plus edge/cloud split for real-world autonomy at scale.

1.title: How to build products on a moving frontier | Dan Shipper (Every)
1.author: Lenny's Podcast
1.hook: Two-track product org model for AI — research lab exploring new capabilities in parallel with product team iterating on current product; tested through live experiments.

2.title: The last roadmap | Claire Vo
2.author: Lenny's Podcast
2.hook: Argues that traditional feature roadmaps push teams to ship without learning what matters, and proposes experiments grounded in customer evidence as an alternative.

1.title: Andrew Ng: The Biggest Opportunities in AI Aren't Where You Think
1.author: Silicon Valley Girl
1.hook: Andrew Ng argues the "job apocalypse" narrative is overblown and claims the real 2026–27 hiring bar is "can you build with AI, not just use it"—with specifics on what that means for non-technical roles.

1.title: Large clusters for small models — Daniel Svonava, Superlinked
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Small models on commodity GPUs can match frontier performance per task; the bottleneck is serving infrastructure — Superlinked's open-source routing inverts the architecture (gateway + shared queue + worker-pulled batches) and doubles throughput.

2.title: Vertical Mobility: Inference from MVP to Trillion-Parameter Workloads — Sitanshu Gupta, CoreWeave
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: How CoreWeave routes agentic inference across heterogeneous GPUs by prioritizing KV cache locality, offloading cache between turns instead of evicting it, and scheduling batch workloads into overnight idle capacity.

3.title: What's New in Inference Engineering — Philip Kiely, Baseten
3.author: AI Engineer
3.hook: Data center inference optimization has shifted to training-time techniques (quantization staying 4-bit, learned KV cache compaction, trained speculative drafters with continuous retraining), with concrete tradeoffs between local and datacenter constraints.

1.title: Are LLM Performance Benchmarks Reliable? — Ashok Chandrasekar & Jason Kramberger, Google
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Google engineers reverse-engineered why published LLM benchmark numbers don't reproduce — harness bugs (GIL, client-side latency inflation, temperature tricks, dataset tokenization drift) masquerade as server performance issues.

2.title: Operating Distributed Inference Systems at Scale — Nishant Gupta & Naman Ahuja, Meta
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: Meta's inference scheduler sees seven concrete axes (GPU generation, KV cache state, tenant priority, latency budget, workflow context) and treats routing decisions as coupled distributed transactions where every hop can fail or timeout.

3.title: Routing LLM Inference in Production: From Engine Signals to Policy — Qianru Lao & Lu Zhang, OpenAI
3.author: AI Engineer
3.hook: OpenAI's inference routing system replaced a feedback-loop proportional controller with a global-view optimizer that minimizes end-to-end latency under capacity constraints, solving oscillation and cache locality problems.

1.title: I reviewed Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol live - and the results surprised me
1.author: How I AI
1.hook: Blind evaluation of Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Sol, and GPT-6 Astra across real work (PRDs, frontend, agents, SVG, video editing) with post-reveal breakdown of what each model actually wins at.

1.title: Building the Document Context Layer for AI Agents — Jerry Liu, LlamaIndex
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Document parsing decomposes into three layers (parsing → semantic storage → workflows), with a hybrid routing between cheap specialized models and frontier VLMs, benchmarked on 2,000 human-verified pages.

2.title: Skill issue: stop deploying vision language models, use them with Skills — Merve Noyan, Hugging Face
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: A toolkit that uses coding agents + VLM judges to label datasets cheaply ($3–4), then trains task-specific detectors that outperform direct VLM inference on latency and cost.

3.title: Inside the Mind of YouTube's Anthony Bourdain
3.author: Colin and Samir
3.hook: Co-founder of Yes Theory discusses how reframing ideas turns unwatched videos into hits, and how to balance positivity with virality on YouTube.

1.title: From Ingestion to Agents: How AI Teams Build on Document Intelligence — Adit Abraham, Reducto
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Agentic systems fail on bad data inputs — Reducto shares specifics on parsing PDFs at scale (token-level OCR corrections, markdown vs HTML tables, evals at every stage) and how structured parsing lifts frontier model performance on benchmarks.

2.title: From VLM/VLA's to Embodied Agents — Armen Aghajanyan, Perceptron AI
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: Perceptron built a unified embodied foundation model trained on a petabyte of multimodal data that trades 10× teleop hours for 10× video pretraining, with a sparse mixture-of-experts router that learns which visual tokens matter per layer.

3.title: MadeOn YouTube 2026 | Creator Roundup
3.author: YouTube Creators
3.hook: Official YouTube platform announcement of 2026 features across discovery, creator monetization, and creation tools — including custom feeds, shorts series, creator partnerships program, shopping integration, and dynamic thumbnails.

4.title: The Best Models Still Reason Like Toddlers — Andrew Dai, Elorian
4.author: AI Engineer
4.hook: Frontier models hallucinate on spatial reasoning (chessboard counting, robot arm state) because they pattern-match rather than reason; Elorian's approach adds visual chain of thought (drawing boxes) and synthetic data flywheels to fix it.

1.title: Modality Misalignment and Originality Attribution in Short-Form Video — Aditya Gautam, Meta
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Three-agent system (perceiver, reviewer, retriever) for detecting modality misalignment and unoriginal content at Meta scale, built on specialized VLMs with DPO training from production samples and human judges.

2.title: AI Engineer Paris 2026 Opening Keynotes: Mistral, Langfuse & Sizzy | Day 1
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: Day 1 keynotes from AI Engineer Paris 2026 covering frontier AI, coding agents, software factories, and economic history applied to the AI moment.

3.title: From Scratch to SOTA: Training a 3B State-Space Vision Model — Krishna Prasad Srinivasan, Sarvam
3.author: AI Engineer
3.hook: A 3B state-space vision model for document AI in Indian languages, trained on a four-stage curriculum including 13T text tokens, that reportedly beats models 100× larger and is now digitizing 35M pages in production.

1.title: Claude Opus 5.5 is Here! Is Claude Finally Back? (5 Use Cases Tested)
1.author: Peter Yang
1.hook: Peter Yang tests Claude Opus 5.5 across five concrete use cases (3D modeling, art generation, design, video editing, computer use) and evaluates whether it passes a personality test that tripped up Opus 5.

1.title: Claude is BACK with Opus 5.5
1.author: How I AI
1.hook: Week-long testing of Opus 5.5 across agentic tasks, frontend prototyping, and safety boundaries, with concrete cost math and model-stack decisions based on real work.

1.title: Pivoting Your Channel - Do This First!
1.author: Creator Insider
1.hook: YouTube's global lead for content strategy discusses channel pivot mechanics — audience ownership, topic vs. creator appeal, rebuild strategies, and audience expectation management.

1.title: Total Recall: Agent Memory and Harness Engineering — Ignacio Martinez, Oracle
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: A seven-layer harness architecture for making LLM agents deterministic, with specific mechanisms — work trees for parallel agent consistency, hysteresis variables for task patience, skill promotion for workflow distillation.

1.title: Meta’s Muse AI Agent Saved Me $800+ a Year on My Bills (10 Real Use Cases)
1.author: Peter Yang
1.hook: Walkthrough of Meta's Muse agent across 10 use cases, including calling customer support to negotiate bills (claimed $800+ savings).
